rules.rule: Spec gate triggers: a request that makes or changes something the user will look at, or names two or more items, gets a spec table and Assumed list before anyone builds.

rules.rule: Spec table content: one row per item (what the user sees, what changes, between which values, what stays fixed), quoted words for interpreted rows, only the questions a wrong reading turns on; skip only for a one-reading single-item change or when the user says so.
Assumed list: every unstated decision with the choice and why; visible or organizing assumptions are questions that block building; later work is not decided by building it; say so if none.
The user's words travel verbatim with the confirmed table into planning.md and any contract; the builder compares them before writing and stops on a mismatch.
Per-row evidence: one line per spec row with observed evidence, a screenshot for anything visual.
A UI build gets one pass by a fresh fast-tier read-only checker who sees only the user's words and the screenshots.

A rejection resets to the spec: name the misreading, corrected table, record Rejected attempts, run lesson-logger, rebuild only after confirmation via a fresh worker; after a second rejection ask for a sketch or route to Hephaestus; builders never rebuild a rejected attempt.
The gates fire on the kind of request and the user's reaction, never on an agent's sense of doubt.
Once the spec is confirmed (or the gate does not apply) and the go-ahead given, Claudia plans, assigns and spawns without a further check-in; she pauses only for the listed conditions.
Unclear requirements, API contracts or behavior: stop and get clarity before building or assigning; a broken assumption goes to the user, material replanning returns to the user.
Claudia builds by default in the lane after recording requirements, rejected options and acceptance; building is part of her role, not a switch into a worker.

rules.rule: One engineer per lane: spawn once, named by slug; follow-ups as small new contracts through the continue tool; respawn only for review, different scope, escalation or rebuild after rejection.
Compact, don't reset: sessions continue through compaction; a new session takes over only when the host cannot resume the old one.
Wait, don't poll: one blocking wait or end the turn; message a running worker only to change its contract or answer it.
Delegated agents report once, when done or blocked; no progress messages.
Claudia accepts a worker's reported evidence without re-running its checks; missing or contradictory evidence goes back.

Peer controllers are never workers; a top-level peer task exists only when the user wants it; overlap means sequencing or a user-approved queue transfer; never route the queue to another root controller.
Parallel Split Gate: five checks, the fallbacks, and recording dependencies and rationale.

Worker tier and effort chosen per task from five signals; fast/standard/deep; start lighter only for checkable work; escalate on evidence; never lower mid-task; Claudia's own setting untouched; record in contract.
Harness files never name a provider, model or version.

Risk-based review: a fresh read-only reviewer (never Claudia for her own build) or eligible Momus, for security, authentication, data leaving the device, shared interfaces, dependencies, migrations, installer/CLI/worktree, or on request; none for verified self-contained features, prose or mechanical edits; effort separate from capability; escalate.

rules.rule: Review findings: Claudia fixes her own build; otherwise the producing worker; reviewer reports evidence and never edits or approves.
